měieach (every)
also: gè

This apple only takes half an hour to eat.

láito come ((used as a substitute for a more specific verb))

māocat

I don't have a cat.

I like cats, not dogs.

lǎoshīteacher
Tā shì lǎoshī.
She's a teacher.
Wǒ shì lǎoshī, zài xuéxiào gōngzuò.

gǒudog

Do you have a dog?
Wǒ xǐhuan māo, bù xǐhuan gǒu.
I like cats, not dogs.

shíten (10)

I sleep at ten.

The plane leaves at twelve.

reveals.html:
lǎoold (of people) (always; (prefix before a surname or a birth-order number))
Zhège lǎo wèntí hái méi jiějué.
This old problem still isn't solved.

xiānshengMr. (sir; mister; gentleman; husband)
Xiānsheng, nǐ hǎo.
Hello, sir.

shuōhuàto speak (to talk; to say)
also: jiǎng, tán
Nǐ huì shuōhuà ma?
Can you talk?
Wǒ tīng péngyou shuōhuà.
I'm listening to my friend talk.

bùkèqiyou're welcome (don't mention it)
Bùkèqi.
You're welcome.

wènto ask (to inquire)
Qǐng wèn, zhège lù zěnme zǒu?

Wǒmen qù zhǎo fúwùyuán wèn wèntí ba.
Let's go find the waiter to ask.
